v.why: If edge 0 is none, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 1->2 adds nothing useful, while with a live node 1 it adds a deeper conv path.
Swapping a pooling op on the input-output shortcut for an identity restores a clean residual, which helps far more than swapping out a conv or none.
Removing the identity residual from input to output hurts trainability more than removing a conv or pooling op on that edge.
Replacing a parameter-free pooling op with a 3x3 conv adds the most capacity, whereas replacing a skip removes a useful shortcut.
Filling an empty edge into the output adds a new learned path, which is more beneficial than replacing an existing skip connection.
Cutting the input to node 1 is costly when node 1 feeds the output through a conv, but nearly free when node 1's outputs are unused.
Upgrading the final node-2 to output edge from pooling to conv adds the most capacity, relative to replacing skip or none.
With no direct input-output edge, removing edge 2->3 removes one of the few remaining paths to the output, so it hurts more.
Replacing an identity on the first edge with a 1x1 conv drops a shortcut that conv-light cells depend on, which hurts more than replacing other ops.
Turning a 3x3 conv into pooling on an output edge loses learned capacity, which hurts more than replacing a 1x1 conv, skip, or none.
